Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

frighten verb

also scare, give a fright, terrify, scare off, scare away, frighten away, put the fear of God into, it makes my skin creep, make someone’s flesh creep

classical

Cic. Fam. 2.16.4: nec mē ista terrent
Traupman 319, 374, 153

terreō, terrēre, terruī, territum

verb, second conjugation

frighten, scare

“Scared” is territus; being afraid is timēre (see be afraid).

Other words

  • perterreō, perterrēre, perterruī, perterritum — terrify, frighten badly

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 5.3.13; Caes. B.G. 7.4 (Lewis & Short)

  • absterreō, absterrēre, absterruī, absterritum — frighten away, scare off

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 2.1.74; Cic. Verr. 2.2.58 (Lewis & Short)

  • terrificō, terrificāre — to terrify

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Lucr. 1.134 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 158

    (Lewis & Short: poetic and very rare)

Examples

  • Nec mē ista terrent quae mihi ā tē ad timōrem fīdissimē atque amantissimē prōpōnuntur.

    Nor am I frightened by the things you so faithfully and lovingly set before me to make me afraid.Cic. Fam. 2.16.4

  • pater deōrum rīsit atque illīs dedit parvum tigillum, missum quod subitō vadī mōtū sonōque terruit pavidum genus

    the father of the gods laughed and gave them a little log, which, thrown in, frightened the timid race with the sudden stir and splash of the waterPhaedr. 1.2.13–15

  • Facit ut horream.

    It makes my skin creep.Traupman 96

See also be afraid, scared to death.
